attacks.claim: The QA table reports the staff pilot as finished with results, but the pilot is scheduled for Nov 2-6 and today is 2026-10-26. The pilot evidence cannot exist yet, so the pass claimed for the pilot gate is unverified.
attacks.evidence: "1. Nov 2-6: flags on for staff cards only (pilot above)." / "Staff pilot week (64 staff cards, real holds) | 0 misdelivered texts; 2 copy fixes shipped and re-verified"

attacks.claim: Batched messages carry one code for multiple holds, but codes are single-use. The artifact does not say whether a batch gets one code per hold or one code for all, and it does not cover holds split across lockers or between a locker and the desk. A patron could be sent to the wrong place or hold an unusable code. QA tests batching only for the daily cap, not code-to-hold mapping.
attacks.evidence: "Riverbend Library: 2 holds ready at Oak St locker. Code 482913, pick up by Sat Nov 14." / "Codes are single-use, expire at the pickup deadline"

attacks.claim: The public announcement promises text alerts 'for every cardholder', but the opt-in is voluntary, requires a YES reply, and is hidden from juvenile cards. The announcement misstates the service to the public, and the rollback has no step to correct or withdraw it.
attacks.evidence: "Text alerts for holds, for every cardholder. 24/7 pickup lockers at Oak Street, Millbrook and Harbor."

attacks.claim: Both flags go live for all cardholders at 09:00, but the smoke test is a precondition only for the 10:00 announcement. Live exposure to all 210k cardholders begins before the stated go/no-go check, and no abort criterion is set for that window.
attacks.evidence: "Nov 9 09:00: flags on for all cardholders; announcement goes out at 10:00 only after a smoke test of one live text and one locker pickup per branch."

attacks.claim: When the SMS cap is hit, every opted-in patron falls back to automated phone calls. Those calls are a per-call cost that the Cost section neither forecasts nor caps, so fallback spend is unbounded and unbudgeted.
attacks.evidence: "On cap, texts stop and every opted-in patron falls back to their previous notice method (email or automated phone call, which stays on file)" vs. Cost: "Forecast 38,000 texts/month at about $0.012 all-in = ~$460/month"

attacks.claim: At $0.012 per text, the $900 cap is reached near 75,000 texts/month, about 2x forecast. A cap hit would move every opted-in patron to email or phone at once. The artifact does not size fallback throughput, define in-flight or queued texts at the cap boundary, or stage the switch.
attacks.evidence: "Provider account hard spend cap $900/month, alert to ops at 70%." / "so no alert is lost"

attacks.claim: The spend-cap QA ran as a $5 test cap against the production provider account in test mode. Production delivery, carrier filtering, and real cap behaviour were not exercised, so the 'no alert is lost' claim is unverified at volume.
attacks.evidence: "Spend cap reached (test cap $5) → fallback to email / phone call | Pass" / "against the production SMS provider account in test mode"

attacks.claim: The remap script is a one-way data change that rewrites pickup_location, extends deadlines, and triggers patron notices. It was tested only on 1,200 staging rows, with no production row count, runtime, locking or batching plan, snapshot, or reverse script. Rollback is the path that must be fast under pressure, so this is unverified.
attacks.evidence: "scripts/remap_locker_holds.sql (tested in staging on 1,200 rows)" / ABSENT: production row count, runtime, locking/batching, backup before remap, reverse script

attacks.claim: The locker_pickup rollback does not say whether codes already issued are invalidated, how cells holding items are emptied, or who confirms every locker item has been moved. Codes can stay live for lockers that are no longer staffed.
attacks.evidence: "staff move items to the holds shelf" / ABSENT: code invalidation, cell-emptying procedure, completion check

attacks.claim: The text reveals hold count and pickup location to whoever holds the phone, and the provider retains message content for 30 days linked to that phone. This creates a phone-to-library-use linkage that the no-borrowing-history policy is meant to prevent.
attacks.evidence: "Riverbend Library: 2 holds ready at Oak St locker." / "it retains message logs 30 days"

attacks.claim: Shared or family phone numbers are not handled. A hold-ready text on a shared phone discloses library use to anyone with access, and the artifact gives no check on number ownership, no household-number handling, and no disclosure of this risk in the opt-in flow.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: number ownership check, shared-device handling, opt-in disclosure of shared-phone risk

attacks.claim: Retention of the phone number, IP address, and consent record is unbounded after STOP or account closure. STOP only clears the opt-in flag. Phone and consent deletion is stated only for permanent SMS withdrawal, and nothing sets a retention limit for the IP address.
attacks.evidence: "STOP ... clears the opt-in flag" / "Phone number and consent record (timestamp, IP, checkbox text version) are stored in the patron record" / "If SMS is withdrawn permanently, numbers and consent records are deleted within 30 days"

attacks.claim: The locker code is sent by SMS to the same phone that receives the hold notice. Anyone with that phone plus the card number and PIN can collect holds, so the pickup credential is exposed over an unprotected channel to third parties.
attacks.evidence: "Code 482913, pick up by Sat Nov 14." / "card number + PIN, existing ILS PIN lockout applies"

attacks.claim: The guardian opt-in path is ambiguous. The artifact does not say whether a guardian receives or can act on juvenile hold codes, or whether a guardian account can claim a locker code for a juvenile card. That creates an unverified authorization path.
attacks.evidence: "guardians can opt in with their own number on the linked guardian account"

attacks.claim: The consent disclosure lacks the standard 'consent is not a condition of purchase' wording, using 'Consent is not required to borrow' instead. Express written consent for automated texts under TCPA/CTIA practice depends on that language, and no conformance evidence is given.
attacks.evidence: "Consent is not required to borrow."

attacks.claim: Locker code and card entry are touchscreen-only. No tactile keypad, keyboard, or switch-access input is specified, so blind, low-vision, and motor-impaired patrons may be unable to enter the single-use code independently at a public facility.
attacks.evidence: "Touchscreen and card reader mounted within ADA reach range (max 48 in)" / ABSENT: tactile or non-touch code entry

attacks.claim: Assistive-technology and audio checks cover only the opt-in web form. The locker touchscreen's screen-reader behaviour, contrast, audio guidance, and text-size setting were not tested, so the physical kiosk is unverified before public launch.
attacks.evidence: "Opt-in form with NVDA + Firefox, VoiceOver iOS; 320/768/1280 px layouts | Pass" / "Locker: card+code, card number+PIN+code, wrong code ×5 lockout + staff alert | Pass"

attacks.claim: Quiet-hours queueing sends held texts at 08:00 with no stated provider throughput ceiling, queue drain time, or backoff, creating a synchronized morning spike.
attacks.evidence: "anything later is queued to 08:00"

attacks.claim: Locker capacity is fixed at 144 cells, and the artifact does not define behaviour when holds exceed free cells or when uncollected items pile up. Staff workload for expired items has no bound.
attacks.evidence: "3 locker banks (48 cells each)" / "returned to the holds shelf by staff next morning"

attacks.claim: No retry, idempotency, or dead-letter handling is described for the send path. A failure during the 09:00 flip or 10:00 announcement could produce duplicate texts that breach the 3/day cap or silent drops that the 15-minute failure-rate alert does not attribute to a patron.
attacks.evidence: "Max 3 texts per patron per day" / "delivery failures > 5% for 15 min"

attacks.claim: The 38,000 texts/month forecast has no derivation from hold volume, opt-in rate, or segment count, yet it sets the $900 cap and the 70% alert.
attacks.evidence: "Forecast 38,000 texts/month at about $0.012 all-in = ~$460/month"

attacks.claim: There is no second SMS provider, export path for consent records or logs, or exit plan for the single SMS vendor and its 10DLC registration.
attacks.evidence: "the SMS provider is an existing vendor under a signed DPA"

attacks.claim: Locker hardware is single-vendor, with no stated exit terms, firmware access, or manual override independent of the vendor.
attacks.evidence: "installed and acceptance-tested by the vendor and branch staff" / "vendor SLA 4 h on-site"

attacks.claim: Data-processing region and hosting jurisdiction for phone numbers, message content, and delivery logs are not stated.
attacks.evidence: "it retains message logs 30 days"

attacks.claim: The legal review cited (LGL-118) is not shown to cover minors, and the teen (13+) SMS option has no stated age-of-consent or state minor-privacy review.
attacks.evidence: "The option appears on adult and teen (13+) cards only"

attacks.claim: No WCAG 2.1 AA or Section 508 conformance evidence is given for the public-facing locker and portal opt-in form.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: WCAG / Section 508 conformance evidence

attacks.claim: Only the English SMS body is shown. Spanish copy, length, and segment count are not provided or tested, and the locker screen and audio guidance have no stated Spanish support.
attacks.evidence: "English and Spanish, following the patron's existing language preference." / "audio guidance through a headphone jack"

attacks.claim: No account-page state is specified between entering a number and replying YES, so patrons may not be able to tell whether alerts are active.
attacks.evidence: "texts start only after the patron replies YES"

attacks.claim: A separate YES confirmation step adds a drop-off point with no conversion measure or reminder, and a patron locked out after 5 wrong attempts has no self-serve recovery path.
attacks.evidence: "5 wrong attempts lock the cell and alert branch staff."

attacks.claim: Pipeline failures are not monitored per patron, so a generated code that is never delivered could cause a silent missed pickup. The alert covers only aggregate failure rate.
attacks.evidence: "delivery failures > 5% for 15 min"

attacks.claim: The 'ADA reach range' claim is stated as installed fact, but the QA record includes no measurement of the mounted height.
attacks.evidence: "Touchscreen and card reader mounted within ADA reach range (max 48 in)"

attacks.claim: The proposal shows no adoption target, patron demand, or after-hours pickup need for the three chosen branches, and success is measured only operationally, not by pickup outcomes.
attacks.evidence: "Dashboard: texts sent, delivery rate, STOP rate, queue depth, locker cell status."

attacks.claim: Two independent features ship in one release and one announcement, which complicates isolated rollback or testing of either.
attacks.evidence: "Both ship behind flags `sms_holds` and `locker_pickup`"
